additions.site_name: Mars Road Data Centre, 3-4 Apollo Place and 87-91 Mars Road, Lane Cove West
additions.name: Mars Road Data Centre — proposed 140 MW data centre (SSD-108835458)

status.summary: On 31 August 2026 the A/Director, Industry Assessments, as delegate of the NSW Planning Secretary, issued additional environmental assessment requirements for the proposed Mars Road Data Centre (State significant development SSD-108835458), modifying the SEARs issued on 9 April 2026 so that the EIS must address the NSW Data Centre Guidelines released on 17 August 2026. The SEARs request describes demolition, consolidation of four lots at 3-4 Apollo Place and 87-91 Mars Road, Lane Cove West, and construction and operation of a five-storey data centre of about 140 MW IT load, up to 37.4 m high, with about 120 back-up generators. This supports an announced project only: no EIS has been lodged and no consent, site work or operation exists.

locator.precision: Project-site marker at the centroid of the 1.50 ha union of the four lots that the SEARs request names as the site (Lots 8 and 9 DP241877, Lot 100 DP622160 and Lot 1 DP732557; 3-4 Apollo Place and 87-91 Mars Road), which the proposal consolidates into one development lot. The marker does not locate the building, the generators, the entrances or the construction extent, and it excludes the strip of 1 Sirius Road that the request says will leave the site before lodgement.
locator.identity_review: The Department's SEARs letters and the consultant's SEARs request name the Mars Road Data Centre, SSD-108835458, at 3-4 Apollo Place and 87-91 Mars Road, Lane Cove West, legally Lot 8 DP241877, Lot 9 DP241877, Lot 100 DP622160 and Lot 1 DP732557, plus part of Lot 1 DP1271404 (1 Sirius Road) that will not form part of the site when the EIS is lodged after a boundary adjustment. The NSW cadastre returns exactly one polygon for each of the four lots; their planar areas (3,470.9, 1,286.7, 2,428.3 and 7,846.9 m2) match the request's lot table (3,473.3, 1,289.5, 2,428.2 and 7,852.9 m2), their union is a single 15,033 m2 polygon (request: about 15,044 m2), and the NSW property register gives each lot its expected street address with exact coincidence (intersection over union 1.0). The partial 1 Sirius Road strip is excluded. The portal's own project point (151.1458, -33.8086) intersects no cadastral lot and lies 34 m outside the union, so it is excluded.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The cadastral service publishes no positional accuracy; the point is a derived interior anchor of a 1.50 ha site about 137 by 190 m (farthest vertex 107 m from the point), and the proposed building's position within it is not georeferenced.

locator.identity_review: Telehouse Canada's article and facility page give the facility address as 151 Front Street West, Toronto. The City of Toronto One Address Repository has exactly one point for 151 Front St W (ADDRESS_POINT_ID 7929376, class Land). locator.uncertainty_reason: The City of Toronto publishes no positional accuracy for One Address Repository points; the catalogue states only that points lie within the parcel or the building footprint, and the footprint and parcel were not retrieved.

status.summary: CDC's investor day presentation, released by Infratil on 16 September 2026, states that CDC has delivered seven large-scale data centres since FY25, 'all of which are now contributing meaningfully to CDC's earnings generation', and lists 'Sydney Eastern Creek 5 & 6' among them; its campus map shows EC1 to EC6 as operational data centres. This records EC5 as operating on 16 September 2026, the presentation date. It is not an opening date and does not establish the capacity in service, occupancy or completion of every data hall.

status_updates.identity_review: The presentation names Eastern Creek 5 & 6 and places EC5 and EC6 on CDC's Sydney Eastern Creek campus. The existing curated project is CDC's EC5 data centre on that campus, identified from CDC's own enumeration of EC5 and EC6 as the campus's two later data centres; its shared campus point is the NSW portal point of the Roberts Road Data Centre consent (SSD-10330; applicant CDC Data Centres Pty Ltd; 17 Roberts Road, Eastern Creek, Lot 2 DP1159804), and CDC's notification under that consent (filed on the portal) names the areas 'including and surrounding EC5 and EC6' as its remaining construction areas after EC4. Same project and campus; no site, locator or capacity changes.
status_updates.successor_review: Strictly newer than the existing 21 July 2026 under-construction observation, which came from a CDC location page. CDC's current Sydney page (sitemap lastmod 30 September 2026, captured 26 October 2026) says 'Eastern Creek has six operational data centres', consistent with this. The Department's SSD-10330 MOD 3 assessment report (high-voltage plant; adopted 8 September 2026) describes the consented expansion as 'currently under construction' without naming any building; it is earlier and generic and does not contradict CDC's statement. Infratil's 7 October valuation update and 21 October Australian data centre update report no Eastern Creek change, and the consent's post-approval Notifications folder holds no later notice. No pause, closure or cancellation was found, so operational is recorded as of 16 September 2026; further fit-out of halls is not excluded.
